newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields pare back after US skirmish.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields pare back after US skirmish.

text.p: *Australian bond yields finished below the day's highs helped by a clarification by Japan's Hashimoto over comments made on Monday which had sent a shudder through U.S. markets.
*Policy easing hopes also help to underpin the market.
Australian bond yields finished below the day's highs helped by a clarification by Japan's Prime Minister Hashimoto about comments made on Monday.
Hashimoto's original remarks had been viewed as saying that Japan would sell U.S. debt in favour of gold if there was not currency stability which had sent Treauries and stocks lower.

But later a statement said these comments had been misinterpreted and that while there had been reasons to sell Treasuries in the past Japan never sold Treasury bonds for profits because of the over-riding importance to Japan-U.S. relations and to a stable currency market.
The local market latched onto the U.S. downturn for want of any other trading opportunities in a market that remains completely devoid of any key domestic events until next week.

However, hopes of an easing in local monetary policy after next week's Reserve Bank board meeting meant that the early sell-off would be short lived, but at the same time turnover remains light until such an event occurs.

"We feel that the recent string of soft economic figures, together with still relatively high real interest rates, provide scope for the RBA to cut official rates again," added Hans Kunnen, chief economist at Colonial State Bank.

The local market underperformed against the dollar bloc, reversing its recent narrowing trend, and particularly against New Zealand. The N.Z. market found a new lease of life from European buying after recently being under cloud ahead of
Thursday's budget and Friday's RBNZ monetary policy statement.
